text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- According to unoficial information, the prime ministers of Latvia and Lithuania may meet to talk about their sea border dispute in the Lithuanian sea-side town of Palanga this Friday. Tomorrow, the Latvian parliament will consider ratifying the treaty between Latvia and Amoco and Swedish oil group OPAB, likely to become an obstacle to the talks.

- NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Atlantic has arrived on a two-day official visit to Latvia. He has met President Guntis Ulmanis, Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs. They discussed the possibility of deepening co-operation between Latvia and NATO.

- President Guntis Ulmanis met with the High Commissioner on Ethnic Minorities of the OSCE, Max van der Stoel. He said Latvia should consider how to solve the issue of 28 percent of its population who are not Latvian citizens.
- Riga City Council is to introduce special licences for the use of the city's symbols as well as for the use of the Riga 800th Anniversary.

- The cabinet gave its first approval to the proposal from the welfare ministry to raise children's allowance from 4.5 to 5.7 lats on condition that income tax reductions for those having children are abolished. The increase will need an additional 10.8 million lats in the state budget.
DIENA
- The statistics Committee reports that in September the monthly inflation rate in Latvia amounted to 0.7 percent. The total rate of inflation over the first nine months amounts to 10.3 percent.

- The ministry of finance is negotiating a $60 million dollar loan from the World bank to pay off the debts of the previous years budgets. It would be a cheap credit due in 17 years at an annual interest rate of seven percent.

- The ministry of education and science will ask for additional founding of 6.5 million lats. The Minister, Maris Grinblats, said the stability of the government will depend on whether the educational sector will receive enough money. Other parties are also to consider amendments to the state budget.
- The Riga City Council approved a list of the first 19 appartment blocks to be privatised.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE

- Although the Cabinet did not take any decision on revaluing privatisation vouchers, it has assigned the minister of economics and the head of the Privatisation Agency to prepare forecasts and calculations needed to cut the value of the vouchers.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- Parliament speaker Alfreds Chepanis has left for a visit to Australia. The vist is aimed at strengthening relations between the two parliaments.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- The Latvian timber industry has protested against plans to reduce and abolish tariffs on timber by 1998. The Latvian timber firms believe this would encourage an increase in exports from other countries at the expense of the domestic wood products industry, which was shielded from foreign price competition for logs by export tariffs.
- The Norwegian group Warner hopes to open a new supermarket in the building of the former department store, Dole, which has been in standstill since the beginning of last year.
